title: Adaptive Lane Bundles: PRD and Degraded-Mode Rollout Checklist for Multi-Protocol Endpoints
creator: Sana Patel
description: Introduce Adaptive Lane Bundles (ALB): a packaging and routing concept that groups compatible endpoint protocols (chat, completions, embeddings, rerank) into tiered runtime lanes. ALBs improve tail latency, reduce cold-start waste, and make graceful degradation predictable. This PRD covers behavior guarantees, telemetry needs, API surface considerations, rollout guardrails, and acceptance criteria for GA readiness.
goals: Define ALB behavioral contract for each protocol (chat/completions/embeddings/rerank)
Deliver a lightweight API extension for tenants to request lane preferences (opt-in)
Implement telemetry and SLO dashboards to validate latency/cost improvements
Provide a staged rollout checklist including degraded-mode fallback matrices and canary velocity limits
non_goals: Re-architecting the runtime kernel selection algorithms (out of scope for initial rollout)
Mandatory customer migrations at GA (ALB is opt-in, defaults remain unchanged)
On-prem packaging changes beyond runtime flags and config schema
success_metrics: P50/P95 token latency improvement of >= 10% for mixed small-request workloads measured in 24h A/B (canary vs baseline)
Per-token cost reduction >= 6% for targeted traffic slices within 2 weeks of canary
Canary rollback rate <= 10% across first 50 customers who opt in
user_stories: As an application engineer, I can opt my endpoint into an ALB so my low-latency chat calls benefit from pooled warm KV caches
As an SRE, I can monitor lane-level telemetry and trigger automated fallback to single-protocol lanes when SLOs degrade
As a PM, I can define canary cohorts and ramp velocity through the Console for ALB adoption
acceptance_criteria: API: Add optional 'lane_hint' field to endpoint config with values [auto, chat-priority, embed-priority, balanced] and documented semantics
Runtime: Requests with lane_hint=chat-priority must be routed to lane with warm KV-cache and achieve target P95 latency improvement in synthetic benchmarks
Telemetry: New lane-level metrics emitted (lane_requests_total, lane_p50_latency_ms, lane_p95_latency_ms, lane_error_rate) and visible in Console dashboards
Rollout: Canary config supports max 5% global traffic, cohorts by account tag, and automatic rollback on lane_error_rate > 0.2% sustained for 5 minutes
Quality: End-to-end tests cover chat+embeddings combo scenarios, fuzz tests for structured outputs, and 1 smoke test script for degraded-mode fallback
Docs: PRD + Console UX spec and API docs published in Confluence and linked from the README
Security: No new data plane exposure; config changes validated by security and compliance (security_review_required = true)
rollout_plan: Design + Spec Signoff (2 weeks): finalize API fields, behavioral contract, and telemetry schema
Implementation Sprint (3 sprints): runtime router updates, Console UX, telemetry plumbing, e2e tests
Internal Canary (2 days): opt-in for internal teams and partner apps behind feature flag
Partner Canary (2 weeks): 10 pilot customers selected with dedicated monitoring and runbooks
Gradual Ramp (4 weeks): 5% -> 25% -> 50% traffic steps with manual gate at each stage
GA: public opt-in release with migration guide and opt-out policy
risks: Resource fragmentation: too many lanes could increase GPU fragmentation and reduce utilization
Unexpected regressions in multi-protocol workloads leading to higher P95 latencies
Incomplete telemetry could hide regressions during early ramp
Customer confusion about lane_hint semantics leading to misconfigurations
mitigations: Limit initial ALB types to three (chat-priority, embed-priority, balanced) and maintain global pooling for small accounts
Auto-fallback: runtime automatically falls back to single-protocol lane when lane_error_rate threshold breached
Telemetry gating: no ramp without lane-level metrics and smoke-test pass
UX: Console tooltips, validation checks, and a migration simulator in docs
